- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% to capture mean reversion.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% for 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% downward bias for 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in the first 7–10 days after a strong bullish sentiment spike; add 2–5% to early forecast values.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., bullish → bearish → bullish), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
